previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and severe chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for malaise after recently discontinuing oxycodone. He had no signs of active infection, with negative blood and urine cultures, and stable chest imaging showing only mild residual opacities. His symptoms improved significantly upon restarting oxycodone, supporting a diagnosis of mild opioid withdrawal. Liver enzymes were mildly elevated, likely due to medication effects, and thyroid function showed a low TSH with normal free T4, prompting no change in levothyroxine dose. His chronic conditions, including sclerodermatous GVHD, lower extremity wounds, and tachycardia, were managed supportively. He was discharged home on a tapering oxycodone regimen with plans to monitor liver function and follow up with specialty care.

EXAMINATION:  CT CHEST W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with a history of recurrent AML s/p bone marrow
transplant now with severe GVH presents with dyspnea and previously had e/o
pulmonary infection // evaluate for progression or presence of pulmonary
abnormalities, infection, vs changes of GVH

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was performed without
intravenous contrast agent and reconstructed as contiguous 5 mm and 1.25 mm
thick axial, 2.5 mm thick coronal and parasagittal, and 8 mm MIP axial images.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence: 1) Spiral Acquisition 4.7 s, 30.4 cm; CTDIvol =
7.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 231.6 mGy-cm. Total DLP (Body) = 232 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Chest CT ___.

FINDINGS: 

NECK, THORACIC INLET, AXILLAE: The visualized thyroid is normal.
Supraclavicular and axillary lymph nodes are not enlarged.

MEDIASTINUM: Mediastinal lymph nodes are not enlarged.

HILA: Hilar lymph nodes are not enlarged.

HEART: The heart is not enlarged and there is no coronary arterial
calcification. A right-sided port terminates in the cavoatrial junction. 
There is a small pericardial effusion, not significantly changed compared to
the prior study.

VESSELS: Vascular configuration is conventional.  Aortic caliber is normal.
The main, right, and left pulmonary arteries are normal caliber.

PULMONARY PARENCHYMA: Previously seen ground-glass opacities in the anterior
aspects of the left and right upper lobes are no longer present.  The
previously seen consolidation in the right hemithorax adjacent to the right
major fissure is less conspicuous, however there is increased atelectasis
along the right lower and middle lobes. There is no emphysema.

AIRWAYS: The airways are patent to the subsegmental level bilaterally.

PLEURA: Trace bilateral pleural effusions are again noted.

CHEST WALL AND BONES: There is no worrisome lytic or sclerotic lesion. 
Multiple chronic bilateral if rib fractures are again noted.  Multilevel
degenerative changes are moderate.  Compression deformity of the fifth and
eighth thoracic vertebral bodies appear unchanged compared to prior study.

UPPER ABDOMEN: This study is not tailored for evaluation of the abdomen.
Allowing for this, the partially visualized upper abdomen is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. Previously seen ground-glass opacities predominantly in the bilateral upper
lobes are no longer present.
2. Previously seen consolidation along the right major fissure has
significantly decreased with increased atelectasis along the right and lower
and middle lobes.
3. Trace bilateral pleural effusions are unchanged.
4. Mild pericardial fusion is unchanged.
5. Chronic compression deformities of the mid thoracic vertebral bodies appear
unchanged compared to the prior study.
6. Multiple chronic rib fractures again noted.
